benchmark: cognition, the withheld family: Wave 1's one look
what: Two runs of the withheld family, each recorded in the ledger before it scored anything. (1) 'baseline': the baseline mechanisms with every Wave 1 setting off, re-run because the recorded baseline's withheld numbers (genesis_baseline.json) were scored before the Wave 1 reviews corrected the scoring; the behaviour is the unchanged system's. (2) 'wave1': each interface answered by its lane's mechanism (mechanisms). Where a mechanism ships off, the shipped system's number is the baseline's. Reported whatever it shows; nothing was tuned afterwards.

scope.plant: simulated: the constants (CONSTANTS: task memory, task length, breach lines) are declared by the benchmark, not measured on the host
scope.wiring: the regulator is called directly with the plant's history; the product's wiring (the gate resources.policy.background_gate, the history file <db>.resources/internal-state.jsonl and the worker's sampler internal_state.record) is not exercised by this family; tests/test_predictive_wiring.py drives it end to end on a staged individual
scope.reading: a gain here is a gain inside this plant; for lane I's forecaster on held-out it comes from reserving memory per background task (removing the trend leaves all of it there; on development the trend matters more: scripts/bench_wave1.py ablations, trend_share_of_avoided)

counterfactual.summary_is: pooled over every group, the front-door questions included: reported, not a claim (the groups measure different things and are never pooled in a claim; see summary_by_group)

self_model.disclosure: lane W printed its describer's answers on the held-out states once during development; the answer key of uncertain_about changed in Wave 1 (summary_original_key is the key the baseline was recorded with)
